chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, good manners elevates its owner to the rank of the fasting one who stands (in prayer).
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for having good manners in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to highlight that moral excellence is not merely a social virtue but a spiritual equivalent to the rigorous acts of worship, specifically fasting and night prayer. This hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on 'husn al-khuluq' as a tangible means of attaining high ranks in the hereafter, often cited by scholars to balance ritual piety with ethical conduct.
